reuse.why: It goes through the shared getScheduledAmount for ranges and the API field, but recomputes the approximate tolerance as Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) instead of calling the existing getApproxNumberThreshold in shared/rules.

duplication.why: The 7.5% tolerance formula is copied from getApproxNumberThreshold; otherwise the rule stays in one function.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts and the API exposes it through scheduleModel, which fits the layering. The approx tolerance, though, belongs to shared/rules.

scope.why: The diff only touches the scheduled-amount rule, its two new op-aware callers, the API model and tests.

maintainability.why: The approximate rule only applies when callers pass a new trailing amountOp, so most callers (balance, schedule tables, schedules app, upcoming list) silently keep the nominal value. The 'roundedMidpoint' option now means 'lowest value', and callers have to pass false, 'roundedMidpoint' positionally just to reach the op.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount re-derives the approximate threshold instead of using getApproxNumberThreshold (shared/rules.ts)

disguised_duplication.where: The tolerance formula is copied inline, unchanged and recognisable.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains a trailing amountOp parameter and an isapprox branch; 'roundedMidpoint' keeps its name but now means min. Only forecast-schedules and api-models pass the op, while schedules/app.ts (2), shared/schedules.ts upcoming list, Balance.tsx, SchedulesTable.tsx (2) and MobileSchedulesPage/SchedulesListItem call it without the op and miss the approximate rule.
